source_title: South Korea fines Google and Apple for forcing own payment systems and delaying reviews - The Hindu
source_excerpt: Seoul South Korea on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) fined Alphabet's Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won ($47.6 million), saying they abused their dominance in app store markets by forcing local developers onto their own payment systems and by unfairly delaying app reviews. South Korea considers $50.5 million fine against Google, Apple over app market practices storyline 1 The Korea Media and Communications Commission, the country's media and telecommunications regulator, spent years investigating the U.S. tech giants for allegedly violating a 2021 law that prohibits app store operators from forcing developers to use specific payment systems. Why did the EU fine Google | Explained Why did the EU fine Google | Explained European Union fined Google €460 million for ‘search abuses’ and €430 million for the Play Store breaches Why did the EU fine Google | Explained storyline 1 The Commission fined Google 42.9 billion won ($32 million) and Apple 20.8 billion won ($15.5 million) and ordered both companies to let South Korean developers use external payment links within their apps and to improve their app review procedures. Google and Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The Commission said Google and Apple unfairly pushed app developers toward their own in-app payment systems while barring payments through external websites. Although the companies technically allowed third-party payment systems within apps, they charged developers a 26% commission and withheld some features available through their own systems, effectively forcing developers to use only their in-app payment systems, the Commission said. Google fights £1 billion UK lawsuit over app store fees in latest Big Tech case Google fights £1 billion UK lawsuit over app store fees in latest Big Tech case Lawyers representing consumer advocate Liz Coll, who is leading the claim, say Google ‌used its dominant position to charge commissions of ‌up ⁠to 30% on purchases of apps through ⁠its Play Store Google fights £1 billion UK lawsuit over app store fees in latest Big Tech case storyline 1 The commission said it also found instances where the companies delayed app reviews without clearly explaining to developers the reasons for the delays or when reviews would resume. It also accused Apple of charging South Korean developers higher commissions than developers elsewhere from 2015 to January 2023. South Korea has for years closely scrutinised the business practices of foreign technology companies operating in its market. In 2021, it became the first country to enforce a law prohibiting app market operators such as Google and Apple from requiring users to use their own in-app payment systems.
